explanation: They grew from Vulgar Latin, the everyday speech of Roman soldiers, traders and settlers. That is why they are called Romance languages, from Latin romanice, in the Roman way.

claims.text: French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese and Romanian descend from Latin.
These languages do not descend from Ancient Greek, Old Norse or Sanskrit.
The Romance languages developed from Vulgar Latin, the everyday spoken Latin of the Roman world.
The name Romance comes from Latin romanice, 'in the Roman way'.

evidence.restatement: French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese and Romanian are Romance languages descended from Latin.
None of them descends from Greek, Old Norse or Sanskrit: Greek and Indo-Aryan are separate branches of Indo-European, and Old Norse is Germanic.
The Romance languages grew out of Vulgar Latin, the spoken Latin of ordinary people across the Roman world.
Romance goes back through Old French romanz to Latin romanice, an adverb meaning in the Roman manner, that is, in the Roman tongue.
